question.text: A call option buyer would exercise the option only if:

answer.text: The price of the underlying asset is higher than the strike price at expiry
The price of the underlying asset is lower than the strike price at expiry
The option premium has increased since purchase

explanation.text: The Logic: A call buyer exercises only when spot is greater than strike at maturity, since buying at the lower strike is profitable. If spot is at or below strike, the call expires worthless and rational exercise does not occur. The Trap: A rise in premium alone does not require exercise; before expiry the buyer can simply square off the option in the secondary market to realise the gain. Note: Pages 68-69 of the NISM Series-I workbook state that a call buyer exercises only when spot is higher than strike at maturity, and page 81 illustrates the same with a USDINR call example. Page 69 also supports the put-exercise comparison and pre-expiry secondary-market square-off.
